abstract: BIS research estimating that 17-36% of workforce skills are exposed at moderate-to-high AI capability levels, depending on the assessment methodology and capability threshold used. The study provides a skills-based (rather than occupation-based) framework for measuring AI exposure, arguing that skill-level analysis better captures the granular ways AI transforms work within occupations rather than eliminating entire job categories.
keyFindings: 17-36% of workforce skills exposed at moderate-to-high AI capability levels
Exposure range depends on assessment methodology and capability threshold definition
Skills-based analysis captures AI impact more granularly than occupation-level frameworks
Cognitive and analytical skills show higher exposure than physical and interpersonal skills
methodology: BIS skills-level exposure analysis mapping AI capability assessments to workforce skill distributions, using multiple methodological approaches to generate a range of exposure estimates.
qualifiers: Wide range (17-36%) reflects genuine methodological uncertainty in measuring AI exposure. Skills exposure does not equate to job displacement. AI capability assessments are point-in-time and may rapidly become outdated as technology advances.
